commit_message:
[Util] Filter non-returning region terminators (#24795)

`Explorer::walkReturnOps` treated every block terminator in a region
branch operation as a return to the parent. For scf.while, this included
the after-region yield that branches back to the before region, causing
loop-carried values to contribute to result affinities.

Skip terminators that do not implement the region branch terminator
interface, as well as region branch terminators that cannot branch to
the parent operation.

Fixes #24787

Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>
name: setup / setup

loop-carried values to contribute to result affinities.

Skip terminators that do not implement the region branch terminator
interface, as well as region branch terminators that cannot branch to
the parent operation.

Fixes #24787

commit_message:
Fix arena allocation alignment at the block boundary (#24773)

This fixes an arena edge case where a request fits in a block before
alignment, but no longer fits after rounding. Such requests now use the
oversized allocation path, and oversized allocations keep their returned
pointers naturally aligned.

Added tests for both boundary cases.

Assisted by: Codex Sol

Instate initial technical steering committee (#24790)

After the recent changes in the IREE community new contributors took
over the steering of the project.

This change instantiates the "Technical Steering Committee" as described
in LF AI & Data Foundation [IREE
charter](https://github.com/lfai/foundation/blob/main/technical%20project%20charters/IREE%20Technical%20Charter%20Final%205-14-2024.docx.pdf)
to make it transparent for users, contributors and maintainers on how
the project is run, whom to ask for advice and who can help moderate
issues.

If anyone thinks this change or list should be changed please reach out.
The PR will be kept open for a few days and will get merged if there are
no blocking issues.

commit_message:
[LIT] Migrate tests lit config to the internal shell (#24810)

Part of #24607, following #24794.

This moves `tests/lit.cfg.py` to the internal shell and drops the
`execute_external` / `force_execute_external` workaround. No RUN lines
needed changes this time. None of the 27 lit tests under `tests/` use
subshells, or anything else the internal shell rejects.

All 27 pass, same as before the change. To check that they still
actually run and aren't just being skipped, I broke a CHECK pattern in
`e2e/regression/globals.mlir` on purpose, confirmed the test failed,
then put it back.

Verified on macOS/arm64 only.

commit_message:
Fix arena allocation alignment at the block boundary (#24773)

This fixes an arena edge case where a request fits in a block before
alignment, but no longer fits after rounding. Such requests now use the
oversized allocation path, and oversized allocations keep their returned
pointers naturally aligned.

Added tests for both boundary cases.

Assisted by: Codex Sol

commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24786)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function
entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.

Assisted-by: Claude-Code

entry block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from
the ukernel call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer
store-to-load forward the forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime
feature check across the enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func
select never devirtualizes and the microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the
actual cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit
patch at the call site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no
stack, so the stack stays bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent
to the (inlined) load and fold as before, restoring devirtualization.

commit_message:
Instate initial technical steering committee (#24790)

After the recent changes in the IREE community new contributors took
over the steering of the project.

This change instantiates the "Technical Steering Committee" as described
in LF AI & Data Foundation [IREE
charter](https://github.com/lfai/foundation/blob/main/technical%20project%20charters/IREE%20Technical%20Charter%20Final%205-14-2024.docx.pdf)
to make it transparent for users, contributors and maintainers on how
the project is run, whom to ask for advice and who can help moderate
issues.

If anyone thinks this change or list should be changed please reach out.
The PR will be kept open for a few days and will get merged if there are
no blocking issues.

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Test AMD R9700

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (javascript)

commit_message:
[LIT] Migrate tests lit config to the internal shell (#24810)

Part of #24607, following #24794.

This moves `tests/lit.cfg.py` to the internal shell and drops the
`execute_external` / `force_execute_external` workaround. No RUN lines
needed changes this time. None of the 27 lit tests under `tests/` use
subshells, or anything else the internal shell rejects.

All 27 pass, same as before the change. To check that they still
actually run and aren't just being skipped, I broke a CHECK pattern in
`e2e/regression/globals.mlir` on purpose, confirmed the test failed,
then put it back.

Verified on macOS/arm64 only.

Signed-off-by: Zohaib Shah <zohaib.shah.2047@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Zohaib Shah <zohaib.shah.2047@gmail.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_byollvm
